# Arbor — Codebase Intelligence & Developer Workbench

> Turn a GitHub repository into an inspectable architecture map, dependency graph, and saved health report. Audits run asynchronously via a background worker or a scheduled daily 03:00 UTC serverless fallback.

Last updated: 2026-11-25

## Key Facts
- Arbor is a developer workbench that produces saved, inspectable architecture and health reports for GitHub repositories.
- The core audit uses Babel AST parsing and explicit static checks. It does not use a generative AI model, so the same input and rules produce the same result.
- Full source analysis supports JavaScript and TypeScript. Stack detection also recognizes Python and Go; Python requirements files are read for dependency data.
- Reports contain derived results (scores, module relationships, findings with file paths and line numbers), not complete source files. Temporary working copies are deleted after processing.
- GitHub OAuth requests `read:user`, `user:email`, and `repo`. Public repositories can be analyzed without granting private-repository access.

## Overview
Arbor helps developers inspect software structure and repository health. Its audits use Babel AST parsing and explicit static checks rather than generative AI. The same source and rule set produce repeatable structural checks; results cover the checks Arbor implements and do not replace code review.

## Key Capabilities
- **Architecture, hotspot, ownership, scan-diff, and health audits**: Summarizes repository structure, dependencies, `git log` churn × per-file AST cyclomatic complexity hotspots, top-level directory bus factors with suggested `.github/CODEOWNERS`, scan-over-scan finding & score diffs from comparable trend snapshots, technical debt, performance, security, documentation, and design-system signals, with schema-validated OASIS SARIF 2.1.0 export for GitHub Code Scanning.
- **Self-hosted or cloud deployment**: Ships a single root `Dockerfile` + `docker-compose.yml` with `postgres` and `redis` Compose profiles, automatic Prisma schema sync, and `/api/health` probes (`cp .env.example .env && docker compose up -d --build`).
- **Dependency maps**: Visualizes import relationships between analyzed TypeScript and JavaScript modules and surfaces detected circular dependencies.
- **Language coverage**: Import-graph analysis covers TypeScript and JavaScript. Stack detection also recognizes Python and Go, and Python requirements files are read for dependency data.
- **Evidence-backed findings**: Shows relevant file paths and line locations for supported checks.
- **Secret and environment checks**: Flags patterns that may indicate committed credentials and identifies environment variables not documented in an example file.
- **Interactive API explorer and documentation**: Includes an OpenAPI runner and versioned Markdown documentation hub.
- **README badges**: Generates SVG repository-score badges for public repositories at `/api/badge/{project-id}`. Copy the badge Markdown from the project report.

## Security & Privacy
- **Temporary working copy**: Arbor uses a shallow repository copy during analysis and removes it when processing finishes. Stored reports contain derived results such as scores, structure, dependency relationships, and findings, not complete source files.
- **Core audit does not use AI**: The repository audit uses AST and rule-based checks. Source files are not sent to a generative AI service as part of that audit.
- **Optional AI features**: Off unless a user adds their own OpenAI or Anthropic API key. Finding explanations send finding details to the chosen provider. Patch suggestions send the contents of one selected source file, up to 64 KB, to that provider.
- **GitHub permissions**: GitHub OAuth requests the `read:user`, `user:email`, and `repo` scopes. Review the permissions on GitHub's authorization screen before connecting. You can also analyze public repositories without granting private-repository access.
- **Token security**: Stored OAuth tokens, personal access tokens, and provider keys are encrypted at rest with AES-256-GCM.
- **Policies**: Privacy Policy at https://arborgit.vercel.app/privacy and Terms of Service at https://arborgit.vercel.app/terms.

## Pricing & Tiers
- **Free ($0 / forever)**: Up to 10 audits per hour, up to 5 members per workspace, up to 3 active scheduled scans, dependency maps, A4 PDF audit reports, and README badges for public repositories.
- **Teams ($15 / month per workspace, not per seat)**: Up to 60 audits per hour per workspace, up to 50 workspace members with RBAC, up to 50 active scheduled repository scans, and merchant-of-record billing & customer portal via Lemon Squeezy.

## How It Works
1. Connect a GitHub repository and review the requested permissions.
2. Queue an asynchronous audit; Arbor clones the repository, parses source structure and imports, and saves an inspectable report. Worker-backed deployments drain the queue continuously; serverless-only deployments use a scheduled daily 03:00 UTC batch.
3. Open the saved report to inspect health dimensions and findings with the file paths and checks behind each result.

## Frequently Asked Questions
- Does Arbor store or train on private repository code? Temporary working copies are removed after processing; saved reports contain derived results. The core audit does not send source code to an AI model. Optional AI features stay off unless you add your own provider key.
- How are scores calculated? Scores (0–100) cover Architecture, Tech Debt, Performance, Documentation, Security, and Design System. Design-system weighting is omitted for projects without UI components.
- What permissions does Arbor request? `read:user`, `user:email`, and `repo`; the `repo` scope is used to read repository contents and, when enabled, to write pull-request Check Runs.
- Are results guaranteed? No. Reports cover the checks Arbor implements and do not replace code review.
- Human-readable FAQ on the site: https://arborgit.vercel.app/#faq
